subjects.name: Language A: literature
subjects.curriculumVersion: Language A: literature guide, first assessment 2021

components.name: Paper 1: Guided literary analysis
components.format: Guided analysis of unseen literary passage(s): two passages from two different literary forms, each with a guiding question. SL: analyse one; HL: analyse both.

components.name: Paper 2: Comparative essay
components.format: Comparative essay on two literary works studied, answering one of four general questions.
components.resources: Closed book (no access to studied works).

components.name: HL essay
components.format: Written coursework: 1,200–1,500-word essay on one work studied.

components.name: Individual oral
components.format: Oral: prepared 10-minute response + 5 minutes teacher questions, on how a global issue is presented through content and form of one work originally in the language studied and one work in translation (supported by extracts).
components.notes: Internally assessed, externally moderated. School-supported self-taught (SSST) variant: 15-min prepared response, externally assessed.

assessmentObjectives: AO1 Know, understand and interpret
AO2 Analyse and evaluate
AO3 Communicate
subjects.gaps: No successor course announced on ibo.org curriculum updates page (checked 2026); last assessment unknown.

subjects.name: Language A: language and literature
subjects.curriculumVersion: Language A: language and literature guide, first assessment 2021

components.name: Paper 1: Guided textual analysis
components.format: Guided analysis of unseen non-literary passage(s): two passages from different text types, each with a guiding question. SL: analyse one; HL: analyse both.

components.name: Paper 2: Comparative essay
components.format: Comparative essay on two literary works studied, answering one of four general questions.

components.name: HL essay
components.format: Written coursework: 1,200–1,500-word essay on one literary work or a non-literary body of work studied.

components.name: Individual oral
components.format: Oral: 10-min prepared response + 5 min teacher questions on how one literary work and one non-literary body of work approach a common global issue.

assessmentObjectives: AO1 Know, understand and interpret
AO2 Analyse and evaluate
AO3 Communicate
subjects.gaps: No successor announced; last assessment unknown.

subjects.name: Literature and performance (interdisciplinary, SL only)
subjects.curriculumVersion: Literature and performance guide, first assessment 2024

components.name: Paper 1: Comparative essay
components.format: Comparative essay on two works studied, answering one of four general questions. Same component as Paper 2 of Language A courses.
components.notes: Guide states 30 marks; the subject brief states 25 marks — guide used.

components.name: Written assignment
components.format: Essay of max 2,000 words critically examining an extract from a dramatic work explored through performance and the student's own staging choices.

components.name: Transformative performance and individual oral
components.format: Two compulsory parts: transformative performance (10 min) of an extract from a non-dramatic literary work before a live audience; individual oral (15 min) explaining the transformation process.
components.notes: Internally assessed, externally moderated. minutes = 10 performance + 15 oral.

assessmentObjectives: AO1 Know, understand and interpret
AO2 Analyse and evaluate
AO3 Communicate (incl. ideas, emotion, character and atmosphere through performance)
subjects.gaps: Still listed on ibo.org DP curriculum (2026). Satisfies Group 1 and Group 6 simultaneously.

subjects.name: Language B
subjects.curriculumVersion: Language B guide, first assessment 2020 (enhanced course first assessment May 2029; assessment model unchanged)

components.name: Paper 1: Productive skills — writing
components.format: One writing task from a choice of three (each a different theme), choosing an appropriate text type. SL 250–400 words; HL 450–600 words.

components.name: Paper 2: Receptive skills — listening
components.format: Comprehension exercises on three audio passages drawn from the five themes.

components.name: Paper 2: Receptive skills — reading
components.format: Comprehension exercises on three written texts drawn from the five themes.

components.name: Individual oral assessment
components.format: Oral: presentation + discussion + conversation. SL stimulus: visual image linked to a theme. HL stimulus: extract (~300 words) from one of two literary works studied.
components.resources: Supervised preparation: SL 15 min, HL 20 min; max 10 bullet-point notes.
components.notes: Duration 12–15 minutes (minutes field = upper bound). Internally assessed, externally moderated.

assessmentObjectives: Communicate clearly and effectively in a range of contexts and for a variety of purposes
Understand and use language appropriate to a range of interpersonal and/or intercultural contexts and audiences
Understand and use language to express and respond to a range of ideas with fluency and accuracy
Identify, organize and present ideas on a range of topics
Understand, analyse and reflect upon a range of written, audio, visual and audio-visual texts
subjects.gaps: lastAssessment 2028 inferred from successor's first assessment May 2029 (Nov 2028 presumed last session for 2020 version). 2029 brief gives no durations/marks; ibo.org says external assessment unchanged.

subjects.name: Language ab initio (SL only)
subjects.curriculumVersion: Language ab initio guide, first assessment 2020 (enhanced course first assessment May 2029; assessment model unchanged)

components.name: Paper 1: Productive skills — writing
components.format: Two written tasks (A and B) of 70–150 words each, each from a choice of three, choosing a text type.

components.name: Paper 2: Receptive skills — listening
components.format: Comprehension exercises on three audio passages.

components.name: Paper 2: Receptive skills — reading
components.format: Comprehension exercises on three written texts.

components.name: Individual oral assessment
components.format: Oral: presentation on a visual stimulus, discussion with teacher, conversation on at least one additional theme.
components.resources: 15 min supervised preparation; max 10 bullet-point notes.
components.notes: Duration 7–10 minutes. Internally assessed, externally moderated.

assessmentObjectives: Communicate clearly and effectively in a range of contexts and for a variety of purposes
Understand and use language appropriate to a range of interpersonal and/or intercultural contexts and audiences
Understand and use language to express and respond to a range of ideas with fluency and accuracy
Identify, organize and present ideas on a range of topics
Understand, analyse and reflect upon a range of written, audio, visual and audio-visual texts
subjects.gaps: lastAssessment 2028 inferred from successor first assessment 2029.

subjects.name: Classical languages (Latin / Classical Greek)

components.name: Paper 1
components.format: SL: reading comprehension and translation on one unseen extract. HL: comprehension, translation and guided analysis on a set of two unseen extracts. One of two options chosen.
components.resources: Dictionary use is part of Paper 1 (students use a dictionary to understand the extract).

components.name: Paper 2
components.format: Short-answer questions on an extract from a prescribed core text + extended response to a prompt. One of four options.

components.name: HL composition
components.format: Original prose composition in Latin or Classical Greek guided by intentions, with a rationale of no more than 10 entries.

components.name: Internal assessment: Research dossier
components.format: Annotated collection of 7–9 primary source materials answering a question on the classical language, literature or culture, introduced by an inspiration source.

assessmentObjectives: 1 Demonstrate understanding of the classical language and texts read in it
2 Interpret and analyse texts through literary, stylistic, historical and cultural contexts
3 Synthesize evidence from primary, secondary and reference sources
4 Construct arguments supported by analysis of texts and other products of classical cultures

subjects.name: Business management

components.name: Paper 1
components.format: Case study based on a pre-released statement (context/background). Section A structured questions (20 marks); Section B one of two extended responses (10 marks).
components.resources: Calculator: four-function sufficient; GDCs allowed in examinations.

components.name: Paper 2
components.format: Unseen stimulus material with a quantitative focus. Section A structured questions (SL 20 / HL 30); Section B one of two questions with structured parts + extended response (20).

components.name: Paper 3
components.format: One compulsory question on unseen stimulus material about a social enterprise.

components.name: Internal assessment: Business research project
components.format: Research project on a real business issue/problem of an organization using a conceptual lens; max 1,800 words.

assessmentObjectives: AO1 Knowledge and understanding
AO2 Application and analysis
AO3 Synthesis and evaluation
AO4 Use and application of appropriate skills

subjects.name: Digital society

components.name: Paper 1
components.format: SL: two of four structured questions on syllabus + real-world examples. HL: Section A two of four structured questions; Section B one of two extended-response questions on the HL extension.

components.name: Paper 2
components.format: Four compulsory source-based questions (text, visuals, data, diagrams, infographics).

components.name: Paper 3
components.format: Four compulsory questions addressing an intervention for an HL extension challenge topic outlined in a pre-released statement.

components.name: Internal assessment: Inquiry project
components.format: Inquiry into impacts/implications of a digital system: inquiry process document (max 1,500 words) + recorded multimedia presentation (max 10 minutes) + references.

assessmentObjectives: Understand, apply, analyse, evaluate and synthesize course topics, real-world examples, claims and perspectives, impacts and implications, emerging trends, and (HL) challenges and interventions
Develop digital society skills: managing inquiry, researching, critical and creative thinking, communicating in multiple modes
subjects.gaps: AOs are not numbered AO1–AO4 in the brief.

subjects.name: Economics

components.name: Paper 1
components.format: Extended response: one question from a choice of three.

components.name: Paper 2
components.format: Data response: one question from a choice of two; includes quantitative questions.

components.name: Paper 3
components.format: Policy paper: two compulsory questions (30 marks each), quantitative and qualitative.

components.name: Internal assessment: Portfolio of three commentaries
components.format: Three commentaries (max 800 words each) on news-media extracts, different syllabus units and different key concepts.

assessmentObjectives: AO1 Knowledge and understanding
AO2 Application and analysis
AO3 Synthesis and evaluation
AO4 Use and application of appropriate skills
subjects.gaps: Paper 1 is 25 marks (caller's prior note did not state P1/P2 marks).

subjects.name: Geography

components.name: Paper 1: Geographic themes
components.format: Per option: one structured question + one extended answer from a choice of two. SL two options, HL three options.

components.name: Paper 2: Geographic perspectives — global change
components.format: Three structured questions (one per core unit); infographic/visual stimulus with structured questions; one extended answer from a choice of two.

components.name: Paper 3: Geographic perspectives — global interactions
components.format: Choice of three two-part extended answer questions, one per HL core extension unit.

components.name: Internal assessment: Fieldwork written report
components.format: One written report (max 2,500 words) based on a fieldwork question, data collection, analysis and evaluation.

assessmentObjectives: AO1 Knowledge and understanding of specified content
AO2 Application and analysis of knowledge and understanding
AO3 Synthesis and evaluation
AO4 Selection, use and application of a variety of appropriate skills and techniques
subjects.gaps: No successor announced on ibo.org updates page as of 2026; calculator rules not found in guide.

subjects.name: Global politics

components.name: Paper 1
components.format: Source-based: four compulsory structured questions on the core (Q1 3, Q2 4, Q3 6, Q4 12 marks per teacher site).
components.notes: Marks from teacher site (MEDIUM); duration/weight from IB brief.

components.name: Paper 2
components.format: Extended response: two essays — one from Section A (thematic studies) and one from Section B (integrating/cross-thematic questions).
components.notes: CONFLICT: IB brief says 1.5 h (consistent with stated external totals 2.75 h SL / 4.25 h HL); teacher site glopopolis.org says 1 h 45 min. Marks (30) from teacher site.

components.name: Paper 3
components.format: Stimulus-based questions on HL extension (global political challenges), drawing on students' researched case studies.

components.name: Internal assessment: Engagement project
components.format: Written report on a political issue explored through engagement and research; HL adds a recommendation for addressing the issue.
components.notes: SL 25 hours, HL 30 hours. Marks from teacher site (MEDIUM). HL oral extension of the old course removed.

assessmentObjectives: Knowledge and understanding
Application and analysis
Synthesis and evaluation
Use and application of appropriate skills
subjects.gaps: Official guide not retrievable; component marks and P2 duration (90 vs 105 min) not verified against the IB guide.

subjects.name: History (2020 version, outgoing)

components.name: Paper 1
components.format: Source-based paper: one of five prescribed subjects; four structured questions.

components.name: Paper 2
components.format: Essay paper on 12 world history topics: two essays on two different topics.

components.name: Paper 3
components.format: Separate papers per regional option; three essay questions for the selected region.

components.name: Internal assessment: Historical investigation
components.format: Historical investigation into a topic of the student's choice; max 2,200 words.

assessmentObjectives: AO1 Knowledge and understanding
AO2 Application and analysis
AO3 Synthesis and evaluation
AO4 Use and application of appropriate skills
subjects.gaps: lastAssessment 2027 inferred from successor first assessment May 2028.

subjects.name: History (new course, first assessment 2028)
subjects.curriculumVersion: History, first teaching Aug 2026, first assessment May 2028

components.name: Paper 1
components.format: Source-based on the five focused studies (paired case studies) linked by an overarching inquiry question; three static questions, all answered for one focused study.

components.name: Paper 2
components.format: Section A: one of two concept questions. Section B: one of two questions on the thematic study, each with a short response and an essay response.

components.name: Paper 3
components.format: Separate papers per region; two essay questions from different regional studies, each evaluating a given argument.

components.name: Internal assessment: Historical investigation
components.format: Investigation in three sections: historical inquiry question; sources and perspectives; synthesis and evaluation. Max 7 sources.
components.notes: 20 hours. Internally assessed, externally moderated. Word limit not stated in brief.

assessmentObjectives: Knowledge and understanding
Application and analysis
Evaluation and synthesis
subjects.gaps: Full 2028 guide not retrievable; IA word limit unverified.

subjects.name: Philosophy

components.name: Paper 1
components.format: Section A: one of two stimulus-based questions on the core theme. Section B: essay(s) on optional themes — SL one, HL two.

components.name: Paper 2
components.format: Prescribed text: one two-part question (parts A and B).

components.name: Paper 3
components.format: Unseen ~800-word philosophical text on a contemporary issue; one two-part question (HL extension).

components.name: Internal assessment: Philosophical analysis
components.format: 2,000-word philosophical analysis of a non-philosophical stimulus.

assessmentObjectives: AO1 Knowledge and understanding
AO2 Application and analysis
AO3 Synthesis and evaluation
AO4 Use and application of appropriate skills

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.curriculumVersion: Psychology guide, first assessment 2027 (first teaching Aug 2025)

components.name: Paper 1: Integration of concepts, content and contexts
components.format: Section A: two compulsory short-answer questions (two of three content areas). Section B: two compulsory application questions on unseen situations. Section C: one of two concept-based extended responses.

components.name: Paper 2: Applying concepts and content to research contexts
components.format: Section A: four compulsory questions on class practicals. Section B: evaluation of an unseen research study with regard to two or more concepts.

components.name: Paper 3: Data analysis and interpretation
components.format: Four source-based questions with quantitative and qualitative findings from one HL extension.

components.name: Internal assessment: Research proposal
components.format: Research proposal using one of the four class-practical research methods to investigate a population of interest; max 2,200 words.

assessmentObjectives: AO1 Knowledge and understanding
AO2 Application and analysis
AO3 Synthesis and evaluation
subjects.gaps: Outgoing 2019 course: last assessment presumably Nov 2026 (inferred).

subjects.name: Social and cultural anthropology
subjects.curriculumVersion: Social and cultural anthropology, first assessment 2019

components.name: Paper 1: Engaging with anthropology
components.format: Three questions based on an unseen text; one question from six 'big questions'. HL adds one question on anthropological ethics from one of two stimuli.

components.name: Paper 2: Engaging with ethnography
components.format: Section A: one question connecting a key concept, area of inquiry and real-world issue. Section B: SL one question, HL two questions from other areas of inquiry.

components.name: Internal assessment: Fieldwork
components.format: SL: observation report, extension of fieldwork, second data collection and analysis, critical reflection. HL: proposal form, critical reflection, research report and reflection.
components.notes: SL 30 hours, HL 60 hours. Internally assessed, externally moderated.

assessmentObjectives: AO1 Knowledge and understanding
AO2 Application and analysis
AO3 Synthesis and evaluation
AO4 Selection and use of a variety of skills
subjects.gaps: Official guide not retrievable; component marks and IA word limits unknown. Structure/time/weights from IB brief (HIGH).

subjects.name: World religions (SL only, outgoing)

components.name: Paper 1
components.format: Stimulus-response: answer five of nine questions (one per religion), at least one from each of sections A, B, C.

components.name: Paper 2
components.format: Two essay questions (from 14) on guiding themes, one from each section.

components.name: Internal assessment: Investigative study (written analysis)
components.format: Structured written analysis based on an investigative study of any religion; 1,500–1,800 words.

assessmentObjectives: AO1 Knowledge and understanding of specified content
AO2 Application and analysis of knowledge and understanding
AO3 Synthesis and evaluation
AO4 Selection, use and application of appropriate skills and techniques

subjects.name: Religion and society (successor to world religions)
subjects.curriculumVersion: Religion and society, first teaching Aug 2027, first assessment May 2029

components.name: Paper 1
components.format: Section A: three questions on a short stimulus (part 1) using studied examples. Section B: one extended response on a short authentic text.

components.name: Paper 2
components.format: Section A: two of four extended-response questions on part 2 content. Section B: one of two concept-focused essays.

components.name: Internal assessment: Inquiry report
components.format: Inquiry into an aspect of religious identity, expressions or experiences of a group/adherents, applying a course concept.

assessmentObjectives: Knowing and understanding
Applying and analysing
Evaluating and synthesizing
subjects.gaps: SL-only inferred from 150 teaching hours and single assessment outline; not yet examined (outside Oct 2026 window).

subjects.name: Theory of knowledge

components.name: TOK exhibition
components.format: Individual exhibition of three objects with commentaries (max 950 words) on one IA prompt.
components.notes: 8 hours. Weighting 1/3. Internally assessed, externally moderated.

components.name: TOK essay on a prescribed title
components.format: Essay (max 1,600 words) on one of six prescribed titles issued each session.
components.notes: 10 hours. Weighting 2/3. Marked by IB examiners.

assessmentObjectives: Demonstrate TOK thinking through critical examination of knowledge questions
Identify and explore links between knowledge questions and the world around us
Identify and explore links between knowledge questions and areas of knowledge
Develop relevant, clear and coherent arguments
Use examples and evidence effectively to support a discussion
Demonstrate awareness and evaluation of different points of view
Consider the implications of arguments and conclusions

pointsMatrix.description: Diploma points from TOK grade x EE grade (max 3). Rows = EE grade, columns = TOK grade. E or N in either = failing condition.

subjects.gaps: TOK grade boundaries (A–E from combined 20-mark scale) are session-specific and not given.

subjects.name: Extended essay

components.name: Extended essay
components.format: Independent research essay, max 4,000 words; subject-focused or interdisciplinary (two DP subjects) pathway. Criteria: Framework for the essay 6; Knowledge and understanding 6; Analysis and line of argument 6; Discussion and evaluation 8; Reflection 4.
components.notes: Graded A–E; contributes to up to 3 diploma points with TOK (see TOK pointsMatrix). Must achieve D or higher. 3 mandatory reflection sessions (final = viva voce 10–15 min); 500-word reflective statement on the Reflection and progress form; recommended supervision 3–5 hours.

assessmentObjectives: Know and understand
Apply and analyse
Synthesize and evaluate
Communicate research
subjects.gaps: Previous EE (first assessment 2018, 34 marks, criteria A–E) presumably last assessed Nov 2026 (inferred). Grade boundaries not given.

subjects.name: Creativity, activity, service (CAS)
subjects.notAssessed: CAS is not formally assessed and awards no marks or points; successful completion is a requirement for the diploma. Students engage in creativity, activity and service experiences for at least 18 months (ideally weekly), complete at least one CAS project, maintain a CAS portfolio (not formally assessed), have three formal documented interviews with the CAS coordinator/adviser (start, end of year 1, end), and provide evidence of achieving all seven learning outcomes.
assessmentObjectives: LO1 Identify own strengths and develop areas for growth
LO2 Demonstrate that challenges have been undertaken, developing new skills in the process
LO3 Demonstrate how to initiate and plan a CAS experience
LO4 Show commitment to and perseverance in CAS experiences
LO5 Demonstrate the skills and recognize the benefits of working collaboratively
LO6 Demonstrate engagement with issues of global significance
LO7 Recognize and consider the ethics of choices and actions
subjects.gaps: first assessment year of the 2015 CAS guide not stated in the extracted text; CAS has no exams.
